title: 一阶有源高通滤波器
statement: 反相放大器的输入支路由 C₁ 与 R₁ 串联组成：C₁ = 1 µF，R₁ = 1 kΩ，R_f = 10 kΩ，运放为理想运放。网络函数 H(jω) = U_o/U_s，电源角频率 ω = 1000 rad/s。
求此时的 |H(jω)|、H(jω) 的相位、从 a 端看进去的输入阻抗模 |Z_in|，并说明电路的高频增益与截止频率。

questions.ask: 从 a 端（对地）看进去的输入阻抗模 |Z_in| = ?
questions.explain: 反相端虚地，从 a 看进去就是 C₁ 与 R₁ 串联到“地”：Z_in = 1000 − j1000 Ω，|Z_in| = 1000√2 ≈ 1414 Ω。它随频率变化，低频时很大。

questions.ask: 高频增益（ω = 10⁷ rad/s 时的 H，取实部）= ?
questions.explain: 高频增益：在很高的频率 ω = 10⁷ rad/s 下 C₁ 相当于短路，H ≈ −R_f/R₁ = −10（20 dB）；ω → 0 时 C₁ 开路，H → 0，所以是高通。
H = −(R_f/R₁)·jωR₁C₁/(1 + jωR₁C₁)，截止频率 ω_c = 1/(R₁C₁) = 1000 rad/s，f_c ≈ 159.2 Hz；本题 |H| = 10/√2 正是比 20 dB 低 3 dB 的 16.99 dB。

hints: 用阻抗形式的反相放大器公式 H = −Z_f/Z₁，这里 Z₁ = R₁ + 1/(jωC₁)，Z_f = R_f。
把 H 整理成 −(R_f/R₁)·jωR₁C₁/(1 + jωR₁C₁)，看 ω → 0、ω → ∞ 的极限。
solution: **1. 网络函数。** 虚地、虚断：I₁ = U_s/Z₁ 全部流过 R_f，U_o = −R_f·I₁，所以 H(jω) = −R_f/Z₁ = −(R_f/R₁)·(jω/ω_c)/(1 + jω/ω_c)，ω_c = 1/(R₁C₁) = 1000 rad/s。
**4. 类型。** 高频增益 −10（20 dB），低频 → 0：一阶**有源高通**，ω_c = 1/(R₁C₁) = 1000 rad/s。注意截止频率由 R₁C₁ 决定，R_f 只决定增益。

en.title: First-order active high-pass filter
statement: The input branch of an inverting amplifier is C₁ in series with R₁: C₁ = 1 µF, R₁ = 1 kΩ, R_f = 10 kΩ, and the op-amp is ideal. The network function is H(jω) = V_o/V_s and the source angular frequency is ω = 1000 rad/s.
Find |H(jω)|, the phase of H(jω), the magnitude of the input impedance |Z_in| seen at terminal a, and state the high-frequency gain and the cut-off frequency of the circuit.

questions.explain: H = −10/(1 − j) = −5 − j5: the inversion's 180° plus the RC high-pass's +45° gives 225°, which is the same as −135°.

questions.ask: Magnitude of the input impedance seen at a (to ground), |Z_in| = ?
questions.explain: The inverting input is a virtual ground, so from a you see C₁ in series with R₁ to 'ground': Z_in = 1000 − j1000 Ω, |Z_in| = 1000√2 ≈ 1414 Ω. It depends on frequency and is large at low frequencies.

questions.ask: High-frequency gain (H at ω = 10⁷ rad/s, real part) = ?
questions.explain: High-frequency gain: at a very high frequency, ω = 10⁷ rad/s, C₁ is practically a short and H ≈ −R_f/R₁ = −10 (20 dB); as ω → 0 C₁ is open and H → 0, so this is a high-pass filter.
H = −(R_f/R₁)·jωR₁C₁/(1 + jωR₁C₁), cut-off ω_c = 1/(R₁C₁) = 1000 rad/s, f_c ≈ 159.2 Hz; here |H| = 10/√2 is exactly 3 dB below 20 dB (16.99 dB).

hints: Use the inverting-amplifier formula with impedances, H = −Z_f/Z₁, where Z₁ = R₁ + 1/(jωC₁) and Z_f = R_f.
Rewrite H as −(R_f/R₁)·jωR₁C₁/(1 + jωR₁C₁) and look at the limits ω → 0 and ω → ∞.
solution: **1. Network function.** Virtual ground and no input current: I₁ = V_s/Z₁ flows on through R_f and V_o = −R_f·I₁, so H(jω) = −R_f/Z₁ = −(R_f/R₁)·(jω/ω_c)/(1 + jω/ω_c), with ω_c = 1/(R₁C₁) = 1000 rad/s.
**3. Input impedance.** Z_in = V_s/I₁ = Z₁ = 1000 − j1000 Ω, |Z_in| ≈ **1414 Ω**.
**4. Type.** High-frequency gain −10 (20 dB), low-frequency gain → 0: a first-order **active high-pass** with ω_c = 1/(R₁C₁) = 1000 rad/s. Note that R₁C₁ sets the cut-off and R_f only sets the gain.
